title: Jones' Conjecture
context_text: Jones' Conjecture was attributed to Kloks, Lee and Liu (2002) and asserts a tight bound relating the feedback vertex set number and the cycle packing number for planar graphs. It is known to be tight for wheels and the dodecahedron. The best prior bound was $\mathrm{fvs}(G) \leq 3 \cdot \mathrm{cp}(G)$.
paper_contribution: Proves Jones' Conjecture for all subcubic planar multigraphs, i.e., establishes $\mathrm{fvs}(G) \leq 2 \cdot \mathrm{cp}(G)$ when the maximum degree is at most 3.

title: Conjecture 2
statement_text: For every planar graph $G$, we have $\mathrm{fvs}(G) \leq 2 \cdot \mathrm{fp}(G)$, where $\mathrm{fp}(G)$ is the maximum size of a face-packing of $G$, i.e., a cycle-packing where, for some embedding of $G$, every cycle bounds a face.
context_text: A cycle packing of a (multi)graph $G$ is a set of vertex-disjoint cycles of $G$, and $\mathrm{cp}(G)$ is the maximum size of a cycle packing; a feedback vertex set is a set $S$ of vertices such that $G-S$ is a forest, and $\mathrm{fvs}(G)$ is the minimum size of a feedback vertex set. A face-packing is a cycle packing whose cycles all bound faces in one common embedding of $G$ in the plane (the embedding may be chosen), so $\mathrm{fp}(G)\le\mathrm{cp}(G)$ and the conjecture is stronger than Jones' Conjecture (Kloks, Lee and Liu), which states $\mathrm{fvs}(G)\le2\,\mathrm{cp}(G)$ for every planar graph. The best known bound is $\mathrm{fvs}(G)\le3\,\mathrm{cp}(G)$ (Chappell et al., Chen et al., Ma et al.), obtainable by a simple discharging argument, while no factor $3-\epsilon$ is known; the authors prove Jones' Conjecture for subcubic planar multigraphs. They pose this stronger conjecture to highlight how little is understood around Jones' Conjecture. The example of many nested disjoint cycles shows that the embedding cannot be fixed in advance, and the discharging argument does not even give the face-packing version with factor $3$ instead of $2$.
